headline: Buoyancy is the upward force that fluids exert—it's why some things float and others sink
universal_truth: What supports you matters as much as what you carry; the right environment lifts you up
fun_facts: Steel ships float because they're shaped to displace more water than their weight—it's about density, not just weight
The Dead Sea is so salty that you float effortlessly on the surface
Helium balloons float in air because helium is less dense than the surrounding atmosphere
discussion_questions: What environments help you 'float' or stay afloat?
How do you create more support in your life?

hook.script: A massive steel ship floats. A tiny pebble sinks. Why? It's not about weight—it's about density and displacement. Fluids push back on objects, creating buoyancy. The right conditions make heavy things float.

cliff.script: Floating isn't magic—it's physics. Objects displace fluid, and that fluid pushes back. What determines whether something floats?

options.text: An object floats if it's less dense than the fluid it's in—or if it's shaped to displace enough fluid that the buoyant force exceeds its weight
options.response: Yes. Float or sink depends on the relationship between the object and its environment. The same object can float in one fluid and sink in another. Context matters.

options.text: Light things float, heavy things sink
options.response: Weight matters, but so does density and shape—heavy ships float while light coins sink...

fact1.title: Displacement
fact1.script: When you put something in water, it pushes water aside—displacement. The displaced water pushes back with a force equal to its weight. If that upward push exceeds the object's weight, it floats.

fact2.title: Density Comparison
fact2.script: Density is weight per volume. If your density is less than water, you float. More, you sink. Oil floats on water. Mercury sinks. The comparison—not the absolute—determines buoyancy.

fact3.title: Environmental Support
fact3.script: In life, your environment provides buoyancy too. Supportive relationships lift you. Toxic environments drag you down. The same person thrives or sinks depending on context. Choose environments that help you float.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: What supports you matters as much as what you carry. The right environment lifts you up. Seek contexts where you float.

outro.script: That's Day 226. Tomorrow, we'll explore how things stay in the air—flight. Until then, consider what environment helps you stay afloat.

growTrack.title: Buoyancy Audit - What Lifts You?
growTrack.activity: What environments, relationships, or contexts help you 'float'—make life feel easier, more supported, more possible? What drags you down? Can you spend more time in high-buoyancy environments? Support systems aren't weakness—they're physics.
